g.text: Cycle 3: the load is in EX and add (in ID) needs x1, so a load-use stall holds the PC and IF/ID for one cycle and a bubble enters EX; sub is fetched twice.

text.style: fill: #222222; font: 8.25px 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: Cycle 5: the load is in WB when add reaches EX, so x1 is forwarded from WB. Cycles 6 and 7: back-to-back dependences are forwarded from MEM, no stall.

text.style: fill: #222222; font: 8.25px 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans'

g.text: Cycle 7: beq resolves in EX and is taken: or (in ID) and and (in IF) are squashed (x) and the PC is loaded with T; xor is fetched in cycle 8.

text.style: fill: #222222; font: italic 7.5px 'Liberation Sans', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Blue arrows: forwarding. Red slots: a stall or a squashed instruction. In BP_MODE=1 a taken backward branch would redirect from ID instead (1 bubble).
